trust or faith and with whom they are in a bona fide manner unable to function harmoniously as a 
team working arm-in-arm with success in the aforesaid three-dimensional sense as their common 
goal. These factors have to be taken into account by the court at the time of passing the 
consequential order, for the court has full discretion in the matter of granting relief, and the court 
can sculpture the relief to suit the needs of the matter at hand. The court, if satisfied that ends of 
justice so demand, can certainly direct that the employer shall have the option not to reinstate 
provided the employer pays reasonable compensation as indicated by the court." 


A division Bench of Hon’ble Gujarat High Court in the case of Range Forest Officer Versus Virjibhai 
Ranchhodbhai & another reported in 2024 (82) FLR 79 has held as under:- 


6.4. The shift in law on this count was highlighted by the Supreme Court in Bhopal Vs. Santosh Kumar 
Seal ((2079) 6 SCC 773] relying on its own another decision in Jagbir Singh Vs. Haryana State Agriculture 
Marketing Board [(2009) ॥5 SCC 327], observing that the relief of payment of lump-sum compensation 
could be a proper relief in a given set of facts and circumstances. 


"In the last few years it has been consistently held by this Court that relief by way of reinstatement 
with back wages is not automatic even if termination of an employee is found to be illegal or is in 
contravention of the prescribed procedure and that monetary compensation in lieu of reinstatement 
and back wages in cases of such nature may be appropriate. (See U.P. State Brassware Corpn. Ltd. 
v. Uday Narain Pandey [2006 (72) SCC 479], Uttaranchal Forest Development Corpn. v. M.C. 
Joshi [2007 (9) SCC 353], State of M.P. v. Lalit Kumar Verma [2007 (7) SCC 575], M.P. 
Admn. v. Tribhuban [2007 (9) SCC 748], Sita Ram v. Moti Lal Nehru Farmers Training 
Institute [2008 (5) SCC 75], Jaipur Development Authority v. Ramsahai [2006 (77) SCC 684], 
GDA v. Ashok Kumar [2008 (4) SCC 26I] and Mahboob Deepak v. Nagar Panchayat, 
Gajraula [2008 (7) SCC 575].)" 

6.2. In subsequent decision in Rajasthan Development Corporation Vs.Gitam Singh ((207/3) 5 SCC 736॥, the 

Supreme Court stated, 


"From the long line of cases indicated above, it can be said without any fear of contradiction that 
this Court has not held as an absolute proposition that in cases of wrongful dismissal, the 
dismissed employee is entitled to reinstatement in all situations. It has always been the view of this 
Court that there could be circumstance(s) in a case which may make it inexpedient to order 
reinstatement. Therefore, the normal rule that the dismissed employee is entitled to reinstatement in 
cases of wrongful dismissal has been held to be not without exception. Insofar as wrongful 
termination of daily-rated workers is concerned, this Court has laid down that consequential relief 
would depend on host of factors, namely, manner and method of appointment, nature of employment 
and length of service. Where the length of engagement as daily wager has not been long, award of 
reinstatement should not follow and rather compensation should be directed to be paid. 
A distinction has been drawn between a daily wager and an employee holding the regular post for 
the purposes of consequential relief." 


6.3. In Uttaranchal Forest Development Corporation Vs. M.C. Joshi [(2007) 9 SCC 353], the Supreme Court 
held that the question of grant of compensation in place of relief of reinstatement could be guided by 
relevant factors to be that whether the appointment was made in accordance with the statutory Rules or not. 
6.4. It is to be observed that the decisions of the Supreme Court have carved out the circumstances and 
aspects which may guide the discretion of the court in awarding lump-sum compensation instead of granting 
relief of reinstatement even if there is a breach of Section 25F, 25G and 25H of the Industrial Disputes Act. 


6.5. These factors were highlighted in Bantva Municipality Vs. Amritlal Harji Chauhan being Special Civil 


3690 THE GAZETTE OF INDIA : MAY 3, 2025/JY AISTHA 0, 947 [PART II—SEC. 3(ii)] 


Application +०.9733 of 2973 decided on 37.3.2944 as under :- 
"(i) The fact that the workman is daily-rated workmen, not permanently employed; (ii) He is not 
holding a permanent post; (iii) Nature of his employment; (iv) Span of service, viz. The period 
during which he worked upto the date of termination of services; (v) Manner and method of 
appointment. Whether it was a backdoor entry; (vi) The time gap from the date of termination; (vii) 
Delay in raising the Reference is also considered to be a germane factor;(viii) Any special feature 
peculiar to the facts of the particular case. 


For instance, in Bhurumal (supra), the Supreme Court noticed that post which the workman held was of 
Lineman in the Telephone Department, and that the work of Lineman was drastically reduced in view of 
advancement of the technology." 


6.6. In the case of BSNL v. Bhurumal, reported in (2074) 7 SCC 777, it was categorically observed that even 
after reinstatement, it is always open to the management to terminate the services of that employee by paying 
him the retrenchment compensation. Even as a daily-wage worker, no useful purpose is going to be served in 
reinstating such a workman and he can be given monetary compensation by the Court itself.” 


Reverting to the facts of the case, as per admitted position, applicant/Sri Janardhan S. Naik was engaged in the 
Powerloom Development Export Promotion Council, Mumabi on the post of Peon and his services were retrenched 
on 26.5.2006 without following the provisions of retrenchment as provided u/s 25 F of the 
I.D. Act, 947. 


Accordingly, as per law, referred hereinabove the workman/Sri Janardhan S. Naik is entitled for compensation as his 
service was retrenched without complying the provisions of Section 25-F of Industrial Disputes Act [947 but he is not 
entitled for reinstatement as prayed by him. 

AWARD 
For the foregoing reasons as the services of Sri Janardhan S. Naik were retrenched w.e.f. 26.05.2006 without 
following the provisions of Section 25-F of Industrial Disputes Act 947, hence, he is entitled for compensation 
amounting to Rs.3.50 lacs (Rupees three lacs & fifty thousand) but not for retrenchment in services. 


The reference No. K-0/I/-/202-IR dated .8.202] is answered accordingly. 
Camp Court, Lucknow. 

Justice ANIL KUMAR, Presiding Officer

ORDER 


This order is being passed on an application of applicant-workman filed under section 2-A(2) of the 
Industrial Disputes Act (herein-after referred as an Act). 


2. The case of the applicant-workman as per his statement of claim is as follows:- 


That he was working under the I“ Party-Management since .05.989 and he was illegally relieved from 
service on 3.03.20l0 by the [7 Party-Management, whereas he had been assured by the |“ Party-Management for 
disbursement of the arrear dues as well as for his rehabilitation. The 7 Party-Management has formulated Service 
Rules and as per the said rule on successful completion of probation on first appointment every employee shall be 
confirmed. As per the rules formulated by the Management the date of retirement from service was 60 years and there 
was no such provision for voluntary retirement scheme, but calling the workman by the Management to submit option 
for VR Scheme was unconstitutional. Though, he did not opt for VR Scheme floated by the Management he was 
forced to sign the format for VR Scheme and he was assured for rehabilitation for his livelihood. Since, the action of 
the Management was neither legal nor justified the 27 party-workman raised a dispute before the R.L.C.(C) 
Bhubaneswar on dated 28.!!.20I3 and when the matter was not resolved he had filed this application under section 2- 
A(2) of the Act with a prayer to pass an order of his reinstatement of his service with full back wages. 


3. The case of the [7 Party- Management as per its written statement is as follows:- 


That the present proceeding filed by the applicant under section 2-A(2) of the I.D. Act is not maintainable 
in the eye of law as the same is grossly barred by limitation. The applicant workman has voluntarily opted for Special 
VR Scheme floated by the Management and the workman has received all the benefits under Special V.R. scheme. 
After that the applicant-workman in an afterthought and with ill intention had raised industrial dispute under section 
2A(2) of the I.D. Act which is grossly barred by limitation. The applicant workman has voluntarily taken retirement 
on 3].03.2009 from his service by way of opting special V.R. Scheme floated by the Management and also received 
all the benefits accrued to him, so the allegation of illegal removal from service on 3!.03.2009 by the Management is 
false, frivolous and baseless. In the Industrial Disputes (Amendment) Act, 20!0 Section 2(A)(2) & (3) are inserted 
for the benefits of the workman to raise his dispute with the management connected with or arising out of discharge, 
dismissal, retrenchment or termination, directly before Labour Court or Tribunal within a specific period of three 
years of such alleged dispute, but the applicant has filed his application much after three years. 


A prayer has been made to reject the application of the applicant-workman on the ground of limitation. 


4. After going through the pleadings of both the parties it is quite apparent that the 27 party-workman/applicant 
has filed this application under section 2-A(2) of the I.D. Act on 28.06.20l6 whereas it is the claim of the applicant 
that he was relieved from service on 3!.03.2009. 


5. At this stage the Tribunal thinks it proper to discuss here the provisions of the Section — 2(A)(3) of 
the I.D. Act:- 


Section 2-A(3) of the Act specifically provides that the application referred to in sub-section (2) shall be 


3692 THE GAZETTE OF INDIA : MAY 3], 2025/JY AISTHA 0, 947 [PART II—SEC. 3(ii)] 


made to the Labour Court or Tribunal before the expiry of three years from the date of discharge, dismissal, 
retrenchment, or otherwise termination of service as specified in sub-section(]). 


6. In the instant case the applicant-workman has raised the dispute under section 2-A(2) of the Act after expiry 
of more than seven years of his alleged termination/retrenchment, so the petition filed by the applicant is not within 
the prescribed period provided under the provisions of the I.D. Act. 


Ts After considering all the facts and circumstances of the case the Tribunal finds and holds that the application 
filed under section 2-A(2) of the I.D. Act is not maintainable as it is time barred. Hence, the application filed under 
section 2-A(2) of the Industrial Disputes Act is rejected and the case is dismissed. 


8. Order is passed accordingly. 


9. A copy of this order is sent to the appropriate government for notification as required under section 7 of the 
I.D. Act, 947. File is consigned to record room.

and as per the said rule on successful completion of probation on first appointment every employee shall be 
confirmed. As per the rules formulated by the Management the date of retirement from service was 60 years and there 
was no such provision for voluntary retirement scheme, but calling the workman by the Management to submit option 
for VR Scheme was unconstitutional. Though, he did not opt for VR Scheme floated by the Management he was 
forced to sign the format for VR Scheme and he was assured for rehabilitation for his livelihood. Since, the action of 
the Management was neither legal nor justified the 27 party-workman raised a dispute before the R.L.C.(C) 
Bhubaneswar on dated 28.!!.20I3 and when the matter was not resolved he had filed this application under section 2- 
A(2) of the Act with a prayer to pass an order of his reinstatement of his service with full back wages.

That the present proceeding filed by the applicant under section 2-A(2) of the I.D. Act is not maintainable 
in the eye of law as the same is grossly barred by limitation. The applicant workman has voluntarily opted for Special 
VR Scheme floated by the Management and the workman has received all the benefits under Special V.R. scheme. 
After that the applicant-workman in an afterthought and with ill intention had raised industrial dispute under section 
2A(2) of the I.D. Act which is grossly barred by limitation. The applicant workman has voluntarily taken retirement 
on 3].03.2009 from his service by way of opting special V.R. Scheme floated by the Management and also received 
all the benefits accrued to him, so the allegation of illegal removal from service on 3!.03.2009 by the Management is 
false, frivolous and baseless. In the Industrial Disputes (Amendment) Act, 20I0 Section 2(A)(2) & (3) are inserted 
for the benefits of the workman to raise his dispute with the management connected with or arising out of discharge, 
dismissal, retrenchment or termination, directly before Labour Court or Tribunal within a specific period of three 
years of such alleged dispute, but the applicant has filed his application much after three years. 


A prayer has been made to reject the application of the applicant-workman on the ground of limitation. 


4. After going through the pleadings of both the parties it is quite apparent that the 27 party-workman/applicant 
has filed this application under section 2-A(2) of the I.D. Act on 28.06.20l6 whereas it is the claim of the applicant 
that he was relieved from service on 3!.03.2009. 


5. At this stage the Tribunal thinks it proper to discuss here the provisions of the Section — 2(A)(3) of the 
L.D. Act:- 


Section 2-A(3) of the Act specifically provides that the application referred to in sub-section (2) shall be 
made to the Labour Court or Tribunal before the expiry of three years from the date of discharge, dismissal, 
retrenchment, or otherwise termination of service as specified in sub-section(]). 


6. In the instant case the applicant-workman has raised the dispute under section 2-A(2) of the Act after expiry 
of more than seven years of his alleged termination/retrenchment, so the petition filed by the applicant is not within 
the prescribed period provided under the provisions of the I.D. Act. 


7. After considering all the facts and circumstances of the case the Tribunal finds and holds that the application 
filed under section 2-A(2) of the I.D. Act is not maintainable as it is time barred. Hence, the application filed under 
section 2-A(2) of the Industrial Disputes Act is rejected and the case is dismissed. 


8. Order is passed accordingly. 


9. A copy of this order is sent to the appropriate government for notification as required under section |7 of the 
I.D. Act, 947. File is consigned to record room.

AWARD 
(Dated: 08" April, 2025) 


In exercise of the powers conferred by clause (d) of sub-section () and sub-section 2(A) of section 0 of 
Industrial Disputes Act, 947 (4 of 947) (“the Act” in short), the Central Government has referred the industrial 
dispute between the employers, in relation to the management of CISR-National Environmental Engineering Research 
Institute (NEERI), Nagpur, and their workman Shri. Pankaj Kishor Bodele, for adjudication, as per letter No. 
24(07)/2023-IR dated 07.06.2023, with the following schedule:- 

“Whether the action of the management of CISR-National Environmental Engineering Research 

Institute (NEERI), Nagpur through its Director and the Contractor M/s Oriental Integrated Facility 
Management Pvt. Ltd. Mumbai in terminating the service of the workman Shri Pankaj Kishore Bodele w.e.f. 
08.02.202] are just, fair & legal? If not. To what relief the concerned workman is entitled to?” 
2. Case is called out. Advocate Mayur Mainde holding brief of Mrs. Gauri Venkatraman has filed his 
Vakalatnama today in Court on behalf of respondent, which is taken on record. None is present on behalf of 
petitioner. Petitioner is not responding and attending the Court since last three dates i.e. 25/06/2024,05/09/2024 & 
4//2024. Not only this, petitioner has not filed his statement of claim till today. Petitioner has not filed any 
evidence to prove his case. Petitioner is not coming since last three dates. It appears that he is not interested to contest 
the case further more. Claim of the petitioner is not proved. So, it is closed. 


Hence, it is ordered. 
ORDER 


The action of the management of CISR-National Environmental Engineering Research Institute 
(NEERD), Nagpur through its Director and the Contractor M/s Oriental Integrated Facility Management Pvt. 
Ltd. Mumbai in terminating the service of the workman Shri Pankaj Kishore Bodele w.e.f. 08.02.202 are just, 
fair & legal. The workman is not entitled to any relief. 


Justice (Retd.) SHIV SHANKER PRASAD. Presiding Officer

In exercise of the powers conferred by clause (d) of sub-section () and sub-section 2(A) of section 0 of 
Industrial Disputes Act, 947 (4 of 947) (“the Act” in short), the Central Government has referred the industrial 
dispute between the employers, in relation to the management of The Director, Visweswaraya National Institute of 
Technology Nagpur, Sh. Patle Contractor, Nagpur and their workman through V.N.LT. Kranti Mazdoor Sangh, 


Nagpur for adjudication, as per letter No. L-420/28/2022 (IR(DU)) dated 29.06.2022, with the following 
schedule:- 


“Whether demand of V.N.I.T. Kantrati Mazdoor Sangh, Nagpur vide letter dated 07.0.202 for 
payment of Bonus for the Accounting year 2020-202 in respect of contract workers engaged by the 
management of M/s Patle Contractors, Nagpur under the management of Visvesvaraya National Institute of 
Technology (VNIT), Nagpur, is proper, legal and justified? If yes, to what relief is the disputant entitled and 
what directions, if any, is necessary in the matter?” 


2. Case is called out. Both the parties are absent. Both parties are not responding and attending the Court since 
9.2.2022. No statement of claim and written statement have been filed by the parties respectively. No evidence has 
been filed by the petitioner to prove the contents of the statement of claim. Petitioner is not coming since long back. It 
appears that he is not interested to contest the case further more. Claim of the petitioner is not proved. So, it is closed. 


Hence, it is ordered: 
ORDER 


The demand of V.N.I.T. Kantrati Mazdoor Sangh, Nagpur vide letter dated 07.0.202 for payment of 
Bonus for the Accounting year 2020-202l in respect of contract workers engaged by the management of 
M/s Patle Contractors, Nagpur under the management of Visvesvaraya National Institute of Technology 
(VNIT), Nagpur, is improper, illegal and unjustified. The disputant is not entitled to any relief.

2- उक्त विवाद, न्यायाधिकरण में रेफर होने पर पंजीबद्ध कर पक्षकारों को उपस्थिति बाबत नोटिस जारी किए गए। नोटिस की पालना में 
met sr द्वारा उपस्थित होकर स्टेटमेन्ट ऑफ sey न्‍्यायाधिकरण के समक्ष प्रस्तुत कर संक्षिप्ततः यह कथन किया गया है कि उसको अप्रार्थी सं. 
4 डिप्टी कमिशनर नारकोटिक्स, कोटा ने दि. 04.0898 को चतुर्थ श्रेणी कर्मचारी के पद पर नियुक्त किया था और दि. 22.09.99 को अफीम अधिकारी 
झालावाड़ के यहां WAR कर दिया था और वहां से दि. 07.08.2000 को अधीक्षक ब्युरो ऑफ नारकोटिक्स भवानीमण्डी के यहां WIR कर 
दिया। प्रार्थी भवानीमंडी में कार्य कर रहा था और अप्रार्थीगण प्रार्थी के कार्य से संतुष्ट थे। well fe. ot.08.98 से लगातार अप्रार्थगण के अधीन 
कार्यरत रहा है तथा प्रार्थी ने दि. 04.0898 से 22.08.2002 तक १2 कलेण्डर माह में 240 दिन से अधिक दिन अप्रार्थगण के नियोजन में कार्य किया 
है। अप्रार्थी सं. 2 ने प्रार्थी को नौकरी से हटाते समय नोटिस, नोटिस वेतन व छंटनी मुआवजा नहीं देकर अधिनियम की धारा 25 एफ के प्रावधानों की 
अवहेलना की है एवं अप्रार्थी ने प्रार्थी से कनिष्ठ श्रमिकों को नियोजन में रखकर प्रार्थी को हटाकर व प्रार्थी को हटा कर उसके स्थान पर नए श्रमिक 
को नियोजित कर भी अधिनियम के प्रावधानों की अवहेलना की है और प्रार्थना की है कि प्रार्थी को पिछले सम्पूर्ण वेतन सहित सेवा में बहाली का 
अनुतोष प्रदान किया जावे | 


3- अप्रार्थगण ने जवाब स्टेटमेंट ऑफ क्लेम प्रस्तुत कर प्रार्थी के कथनों का प्रतिवाद किया है कि प्रार्थी श्रमिक द्वारा प्रस्तुत क्लेम विधि संगत 
नहीं है क्योंकि प्रतिपक्षी अधिनियम में परिभाषित उद्योग की परिभाषा में नहीं आता है, न ही प्रार्थी श्रमिक के पक्ष में ऐसा कोई वाद उत्पन्न हुआ है 
जिसके आधार पर यह प्रस्तुत प्रकरण को न्यायाधिकरण के सम्मूख प्रस्तुत कर सके। प्रार्थी द्वारा किए गए कार्य एक अस्थाई प्रकृति का आकस्मिक 
कार्य था तथा अप्रार्थगण के विभाग में आकस्मिक कार्य की जरूरत होने पर प्रार्थी को कुछ समय के लिए रखा गया था अप्रार्थीगण द्वारा सेस कभी 
भी नियमित नियुक्ति प्रदान नहीं की गई न ही कभी उसे सेवा मुक्त किया गया। प्रार्थी को जब अप्रार्थी विभाग द्वारा नियुक्ति ही नहीं दी गई, तो उसे 
सेवा मुक्त किए जाने का प्रश्न ही उत्पन्न नहीं होता है। अप्रार्थगण का कार्य सोवरण फंक्शन ऑफ दी स्टेट का कार्य है। प्रार्थी की चतुर्थ श्रेणी 
कर्मचारी के पद पर नियुक्ति कभी भी नहीं की गई बल्कि उसे कार्य की आकस्मिक आवश्यकता होने पर कुछ समय के लिए एक कार्य विषेश को 
सम्पादित करने के लिए दैनिक भुगतान के आधार पर रखा गया था और कार्य पूरा होने पर उसकी सेवा स्वतः समाप्त हो गई थी। कानूनन प्रार्थी व 
अप्रार्थीगण के मध्य कर्मकार एवं नियोजक का संबंध उत्पन्न नहीं हुआ। प्रार्थी के प्रकरण में अधिनियम के प्रावधान लागू नहीं होते है। इसलिए प्रार्थी 
कोई अनुतोष पाने का अधिकारी नहीं है एवं प्रार्थी का क्लेम प्रार्थना पत्र निरस्तनीय है।

0/04/2022 4 प्रतिपादित सिद्धांतों से मार्गदर्शन प्राप्त किया गया है जिसमें प्रकट किया गया अभिमत निम्नानुसार हैः- 


"The Division Bench of this Court in the case of Deputy Conservator of Forests & Anr. Vs. Sharfuddin (DB 
Special Appal Writ No.700/208) decided on 20.08.209 has held as under in Para Nos. 3 and 4:- 


"3. We have heard counsel for the parties. It is contended by the State that the approach of the Courts these 
days has been to not direct reinstatement but instead grant lump sum compensation; the decision in the Director, Tiger 
Project, Sariska, District Alwar Vs. Data Ram and Ors.- DB. Special Appeal Writ No.406/20I8 and connected cases 
on 3.07.208 has been cited. It is contended that in that judgment Court had directed that broadly if someone had 
worked for a year, the compensation payable would be Rs.!,00,000/-; in the case of two years, it ought to have been 
Rs.2,00,000/- and in the case of three years and above, it ought to be Rs.3,00,000/-. Counsel for the respondent argued 
that the Labour Court itself had denied back wages. In these circumstances, the denial of reinstatement would 
be unfair. 


4. Having considered the overall circumstances and the given facts of this case which clearly shows that the 
workman was in service for one year, in the opinion of this Court, the ends of justice would be served if lum sum 
compensation to the tune of Rs.2,50,000/- (approximately equivalent to two years back wages) based on minimum 
wages is given. Thus amount shall be paid to the respondent within eight weeks from today." 


Considering the facts and circumstances of the case and more particularly the view of the Hon'ble Supreme 
Court that reinstatement is not automatic in such matters and taking into consideration the view taken by the Division 
Bench of this Court in the case of Deputy Conservator of Forests (supra), I am of the view that the findings recorded 
by the Labour Court do not require interference by this Court. However, considering that the reinstatement is not 
automatic, I deem it just and proper to award compensation of Rs.3 Lakhs to the workman in lieu of reinstement. 

Accordingly, the employer is directed to pay an amount of Rs. 3 Lakhs to the workman respondent as 
compensation in lieu of reinstatement as observed about within a period of two months from the date of receipt of a 
certified copy of this order. 


The award of the Labour Court dated 30.04.2008 is modified in the above terms."

AWARD 


In exercise of powers conferred under clause (d) of Sub-section (l) and Sub-section (2A) of Section l0 of the 
Industrial Disputes Act, 947 (4 of 947), the Government of India through the Ministry of Labour, vide its Order 
No. L-2202/07/2022-IR(CM-ID dated 0.02.2022 has been pleased to refer the following dispute between the 
employer, that is the Management of Kumardihi ‘B’ Colliery under Bankola Area of Eastern Coalfields Limited and 
their workman for adjudication by this Tribunal. 


SCHEDULE 


“ Whether the action of the Management of M/s. Eastern CoalfieldsLtd. in relation to its Kumardihi B Colliery 
under Bankola Area in imposing a punishment of dismissal on Shri Arjun Bouri, Ex- U.G. Loader (U.M. 
49289) Kumardihi B Colliery under Bankola Area w.e.f. /9-94 2020 is just and legal? If not, to what relief 
the workman is entitled to? ” 


l. On receiving Order No. L-2202/07/2022-IR(CM-II) dated 0.02.2022from the Government of India, Ministry of 
Labour, New Delhi for adjudication of the dispute, a Reference case was registered on 0.02.2022 / 0.07.2022 andan 
order was passed for issuing notice to the parties through registered post, directing them to appear and submit their 
written statements along withrelevant documents in support of their claims. 


374 THE GAZETTE OF INDIA : MAY 3], 2025/JY AISTHA 0, 947 [PART II—SEC. 3(ii)] 


2. The union of Koyala Mazdoor Congress filed written statement on0I.!.2022 on behalf of Arjun Bouri through the 
President of the union. Management contested the case by filing the written statement on 7.0!.2023. In nutshell, the 
fact ofthe case as disclosed in the written statement of the union is that Arjun Bouri was employed at Kumardihi (37 
Colliery under Bankola Area of Eastern Coalfields Limited (hereinafter referred to as ECL) as an Underground 
Loader, bearing U.M. No. !9280. He could not attend his duty due to illness and after recovery from illness he 
reported for duty and submitted his medicaldocuments before the Manager of the Colliery but the management did 
notallow him to join his duty and issued a Charge Sheet dated 8/2!.05.2007 imputing the charge of unauthorized 
absence from 04.0.2006 to 8.05.2007 i.e., for a period of seven (7) months and fourteen (4) days. Arjun Bouri 
replied to the Charge Sheet and requested the management to allow him to join his duty. The management of the 
Colliery initiated a Domestic Enquiry Proceeding. The workman participated in the enquiry and disclosed the reasons 
that he wasabsent due to his illness and also submitted documents related to his medicaltreatment. After completion of 
the Enquiry Proceeding, the General Manager ofBankola Area dismissed the workman from his service by issuing a 
letter bearing Ref. No. BA/PD/DIS/992 dated 7/9.04.20l0. After receiving theorder of dismissal, Arjun Bouri 
submitted Mercy Appeal before the management of ECL Headquarters, once again disclosing the reason for his 
absence fromduty. The mercy appeal was considered in the light of the Memorandum of Settlement signed before the 
Regional Labour Commissioner (Central), Asansolon 22.05.2007, wherein it was laid down that if a workman 
remained absent fora period up to nine (9) months and his age was below forty-five (45) years, then the mercy appeal 
would be considered. According to the union, competent authority of the management of ECL approved reinstatement 
of Arjun Bouri andcommunicated the same to the Area but did not inform Arjun Bouri. The Area Medical Officer was 
requested to arrange for medical examination of ArjunBouri before his reinstatement but the date of medical 
examination was not communicated to the workman deliberately. The union under suchcircumstance raised the 
Industrial Dispute before the Assistant Labour Commissioner (Central), Raniganj and during conciliation 
management agreedto consider the mercy appeal and to process the proposal for his reinstatement. The management 
of the Colliery initiated the proposal for re-validation of the order of reinstatement of Arjun Bouri issued by the Sr. 
Manager (P/L&IR), ECL vide Ref. No. ECL/CMD/C-6B/IL/Il/DA/799dated 3.08.20I. The proposal was then sent 
to the ECL Headquarters but no action has been taken till date. Further contention of the union is that the management 
awarded highest and extreme punishment upon Arjun Bouri which is not proportionate to the nature of charge 
levelled against him. Union prayed for issuing necessary direction upon the management to issue an order approving 
reinstatement of Arjun Bouri and payment of back wages with all other consequential benefits. 


3. Management contested the Industrial Dispute contending interalia that enquiry was conducted against the 
workman, who took part against the Enquiry Proceeding. After careful perusal of the report and past attendance of the 
workman the concerned authority issued a second Show Cause Notice to the workman. The General Manager of 
Bankola Area thereafter dismissed Arjun Bouri by issuing a letter dated 7/9.04.200. It is further contended that the 
union has raised the Industrial Dispute after lapse of several years, without explaining the delay. It is urged that the 
dismissal of Arjun Bouri was justified and he is not entitled to any relief. 


4. In the instant case Arjun Bouri has filed his affidavit-in-chief and he is crossexamined as Workman Witness No. |. 
He has filed the following documents in support of his case : 


(i) Copy of the Identity Card of Arjun Bouri issued by ECL has been marked as Exhibit ४-।. 
(ii) Copy of the Charge Sheet dated 8/2.05.2007, as Exhibit W-2. 


(iii) Copy of the letter of dismissal dated 3/24.05.200 issued by the Agent, Kumardihi ‘B’ Colliery, as 
Exhibit W-3. 


(iv) Copy of the Application of Arjun Bouri dated 02.04.200 seeking reinstatement, as Exhibit W-4. 
(v) Copy of the Mercy Appeal of Arjun Bouri dated 28.05.204, as Exhibit W-5. 
(vi) Copy of another Mercy Appeal of ad dated 29.2.204, as Exhibit W-6. 


(vii)Copy of the written statement submitted by the management before the Regional Labour Commissioner (Central), 
Asansol in connection with dismissal of Arjun Bouri, as Exhibit W-7. 


5.In cross-examination the witness denied the suggestion that he was a habitual absentee in service. The witness 
admitted that he attended duty for one hundred forty-four days only in the year 2003, in the year 2004 his attendance 
was nil and forty-seven days only in the year 2005. It transpires from his crossexamination that the workman had 
remained absent from his duty as he was harassed by money lenders due to his failure in re-payment and at the 
relevant time, he had run away from his village without informing the management. The workmanafter receiving the 
Charge Sheet, participated in the enquiry and received Enquiry Report and findings. It transpires fromhis evidence 
that no second Show Cause Notice was served upon him. The witness admitted his signature on an application 
submitted by him which has been marked as Exhibit १४-4/, He also identified his signature as Exhibit W-5/I on 
amercy appeal. It is gathered from his evidence that after his dismissal the workman requested the union to submit his 
mercy appeal. The witness denied the suggestion of the management that he had been notified by the management to 
report for medical examination after his dismissal. It is also evident from his testimony that witness did not withdraw

his Provident Fund dues and Gratuity amount lying with the company. 


6.Management filed an affidavit-in-chief of Mr. Anuj Lakra, Deputy Manager (Personnel), Kumardihi 87 Colliery 
who is examined by the management as Management Witness No. |. Management produced the following

workman and their outcome is collectively marked as Exhibit M-5.

(P), Bankola Area regarding non-appearance of Arjun Bouri before the Area Medical Officer, as Exhibit M-6.

considered by the management on the basis of mutual agreement in Form-H, as Exhibit M-7.

7. In course of cross-examination the management witness was unable to produce any document that management 
took any step to honour the agreement. course of cross-examination the management witness admitted that he was 
unable to produce any document showing service of second Show Cause Notice upon the workman. The witness 
admitted that after dismissal of the workman he submitted prayer for reinstatement in service and the same was 
considered by the management. The witness also deposed that by the letter dated 20.08.20ll the workman was 
referred for medical examination in connection to his reinstatement in service. A copy of the letter is marked as 
Exhibit M-0. The letter was served upon the workman. The witness however stated that no further dated was fixed 
for medical examination of the workman and that in letter dated 20.08.20l! management of Bankola Area requested 
the Medical Officer to hold medical examination of the ex-employees including Arjun Bouri. Management witness 
deposed that he is unable to state the date fixed for medical examination nor could he produce any copy of Notice 
issued to the workman informing dated of his medical examination. The management witness admitted the fact that 
on 04.2.20l3 a Memorandum of Settlement between the management and union was entered to resolve the dispute 
finally but management 


8. In the backdrop of the facts and circumstances, pleadings of the parties and the evidence adduced by the respective 
witnesses, the moot question which requires adjudication is whether the punishment of dismissal of Arjun Bouri 
w.e.f. 9.04.2020 is justified and legal and to what relief the workman is entitled to? 


9. Mr. Rakesh Kumar, Union representative arguing the case on behalf of the dismissed workman submitted that 
Arjun Bouri was absent from his duty for less than nine months, due to his illness and at the relevant time he was less 
than forty-five years of age. Referring to the charge of unauthorized and habitual absence from duty levelled against 
the workman, it is argued that the charged employee submitted reply to the Charge Sheet wherein he cited the reason 
for his absence that due to harassment and fear of the money lenders at the workplace he could not attend work. The 
reason was not found satisfactory and an enquiry was initiated. The workman was found guilty of the charge under 
Clause 26.23 and 26.29 of the Certified Standing Orders applicable to the management and workman. Therefore, the 
punishment of his dismissal from service was disproportionate to the charge. The union representative further argued 
that after dismissal of the workman by the Competent Authority the workman submitted a Mercy Appeal for 
reinstatement in service which was considered and an order dated 3.08.20ll was passed by the Sr. Manager 
(P/L&IR), ECL (Exhibit M-7), whereby the Competent Authority approved reinstatement of Arjun Bouri preceded by 
reexamination of the records of the Colliery to find out whether the age of the ex-employee was below the age of 
forty-five years on the date of application and the total period of absence was less than nine months. It is argued that 
on 20.08.20, the Sr. Manager (P)/IC, Bankola Area issued a letter to the Medical Officer for arranging medical 
examination of Arjun Bouri of Kumardihi ‘B’ Colliery and the document has been produced by the management as 
(Exhibit M-I0). It is further argued that since 20.08.20l! no communication was made to the dismissed workman, 
informing him any specific date for holding his medical examination. It is urged on behalf of the workman that there 
was deliberate silence and inaction of the management in disposing the matter for which a complaint was made and a 
Memorandum of Settlement was made in Form-H on 4.!2.20l3 (Exhibit M8) where the management agreed before 


376 THE GAZETTE OF INDIA : MAY 3], 2025/JY AISTHA 0, 947 [PART II—SEC. 3(ii)] 


the Assistant Labour Commissioner (Central), Raniganj regarding implementation of settlement within thirty days 
from the date of settlement but no such settlement took place. Mr. Rakesh Kumar argued that the management has 
miserably failed to produce any evidence to show that the management had adopted any procedure for medical 
examination or for verifying the age of the workman at the time of his mercy appeal. It is vehemently argued that at 
this stage when the Competent Authority of ECL has accepted the prayer for reinstatement of the workman according 
to Memorandum of Settlement dated 22.05.2007, the question of legality of dismissal does not arise and the workman 
should be accommodated by way of setting aside the order of dismissal and reinstatement in service. 


0.Mr. P. K. Das, learned advocate for the management, in reply, argued that ample opportunity was given to the 
workman for appearing before the Medical Board but he did not avail the same. Referring to an application dated 
6.07.20i4 (Exhibit M9) submitted by Arjun Bouri, learned advocate argued that the workman was aware about the 
requirement of his appearance before the Medical Officer but he did not comply the same. Learned advocate further 
argued that the workman is a habitual absentee and participated in the Enquiry Proceeding, therefore he is not entitled 
to any relief against the order of dismissal passed by the Competent Authority. |.Having considered the arguments 
advanced by the learned advocate for the management and the union representative, it appears that the point of 
contention boils down to the question as to whether Arjun Bouri fulfilled the criteria for reinstatement as laid down in 
the Memorandum of Settlement dated 22.05.2007. It is explicit from Exhibit M-7 a letter dated 3.08.20I that the 
Competent Authority had favorably re-considered the case of Arjun Bouri for his reinstatement in service at 
Kumardihi 87 Colliery under Bankola Area of ECL if he fulfilled the conditions that his total period of his absence 
from duty was below nine (9) months and the concerned employee was below the age of forty-five (45) years at the 
time of filing his Mercy application. Copy of the decision was addressed to the Sr. Manager (P/Estb.), ECL 
Headquarters. The Sr. Manager (P)/IC, Bankola Area, in his turn, issued a letter to the Medical Officer requesting him 
to arrange for medical examination of Arjun Bouri along with others. The letter has been produced asExhibit 
॥|0. The management of ECL has miserably failed to prove that any concrete measure has been taken by the manage 
ment of ECL at Bankola Area to implement the decision of Competent Authority of ECL. No letter has been produced 
by the management to prove that they had informed Arjun Bouri to appear for his medical examination before any H 

ospital or Medical Board on any particular date for determining his medical fitness. The age of the workman is alread 

y available with the management in the Service Record of the concerned exemployee. There is no iota of evidence to 
show that the management has made any sincere effort to comply its own Memorandum of Settlement. It is a well 
settled principle that parties entering into a settlement are bound to comply its terms. I therefore, find that it is a fit 
case where the management of Kumardihi ‘B’ Colliery, ECL should take immediate measure to determine whether 
Arjun Bouri was within forty-five (45) years of age on the date of his submitting the mercy appeal. So far as the 
period of absence is concerned it can be deduced from the Charge Sheet that the period of his absence was only seven 
(7) months and fourteen ([4) days, which is less than the maximum period of nine months. Under the facts and 
circumstances of the case I hold that Competent Authority of ECL, having decided to re-consider the case of Arjun 
Bouri for his reinstatement in service, the letter of dismissal dated 7/9.04.200 (Exhibit M-4) is not found valid and 
legally tenable and the same is set aside. The management of ECL is directed to take necessary step to reinstate Arjun 
Bouri in service within one month from the date of communication of this Award. In view of the facts and 
circumstances of the case I am not inclined to allow any back wages to the workman during the period of his absence 
from duty. However, the period of absence shall be considered as dies-non for the purpose of maintaining continuity 
of his service. The management of ECL is directed to pay fifty percent (50%) of the back wages to the workman from 


3.08.20Il when the Competent Authority approved the prayer for reinstatement, till date. 
Hence, 
ORDERED 


that the Industrial Dispute is allowed on contest. The order of dismissal passed against Arjun Bouri bearing Ref. No. 
BA/PD/DIS/992 dated 7/9.04.200 is arbitrary, not found legally tenable and the same is set aside. The managemen 
t of Kumardihi “B’ Colliery under Bankola Area of Eastern Coalfields Limited is directed to take necessary steps for 
reinstatement of Arjun Bouri in his service within one month from the date of communication of the Award. The wo 
rkman is not entitled to any back wages for the period of absence from his duty till 3.08.20l! when the Competent A 
uthority approved reinstatement of the workman and the period of absence is treated as diesnon. The management of 
Eastern Coalfields Limited shall pay back wages to the workman from 3.08.20I till his reinstatement in employmen 
t at the rate of fifty percent (50%) of his wages. Let an award be drawn up in light of my above findings. Let copies of 
the Award in duplicate be sent to the Ministry of Labour and Employment, Government of India, New Delhi for infor 
mation and Notification

Sushil Bouri 
Vs. 


Management of Sonepur Bazari Project, ECL 


REPRESENTATIVES: 

For the Union/Workman: Mr. Rakesh Kumar, President, Koyala Mazdoor Congress. 
For the Management of ECL: Mr. P. K. Das, Advocate.

AWARD 


In exercise of powers conferred under clause (9) of Sub-section (l) and Sub-section (2A) of Section 0 of 
the Industrial Disputes Act, 947 (4 of 947), the Government of India through the Ministry of Labour, vide its 
OrderNo. L 2202/ 2/2022-IR(CM-II) dated 5.03.2022 has been pleased to refer the scheduled dispute between 
the employer, that is the Management of Sonepur Bazari Project under Sonepur Bazari Area of Eastern Coalfields 
Limited and their workman for adjudication by this Tribunal. 


SCHEDULE 


“Whether the demand raised by Koyala Mazdoor Congress (HMS), Asansol in respect of Sri Sushil Bouri, 
who worked under the management of Sonepur Bazari Project, Sonepur Area of M/s. E.C.Ltd., Paschim 
Burdhaman, West Bengal, for reinstatement in service through the letter dated /3/05/29/4 is legal, proper 
and justified? If yes, to what relief the workman is entitled to? ” 


l. On receiving Order No. L-2202/2/2022-IR(CM-ID) dated 5.03.2022 from the Government of India, Ministry of 
Labour, New Delhi for adjudication of the dispute, a Reference case was registered on 29.03.2022 / 0.07.2022 and 
an order was passed for issuing notice to the parties through registered post, directing them to appear and submit their 
written statements along with relevant documents in support of their claims. 


2.Sushil Bouri the dismissed workman filed written statement in this case on 23.0.2023 through Mr. Rakesh Kumar, 


378 THE GAZETTE OF INDIA : MAY 3], 2025/JY AISTHA 0, 947 [PART II—SEC. 3(ii)] 


President, Koyala Mazdoor Congress. The management of Sonepur Bazari Project under Sonepur Bazari Area of 
Eastern Coalfields Limited (hereinafter referred to as ECL) also filed their written statement on the same 
date i.e., 23.0.2023. The fact of the case, as disclosed in the written statement of the workman is that Sushil Bouri 
was 


posted as E.P. Helper (U.M. No. 7064]) at Sonepur Bazari Project under Sonepur Bazari Area of ECL. He was 
unable to attend his duty from 2!.2.995 due to illness. He reported to join his duty but the management of Sonepur 
Bazari Project did not consider his request and issued a Charge Sheet against him bearing Ref. 
No. ECL/SBP/Pers/95/23 dated /3.04.996. The workman replied to the Charge Sheet disclosing that he was 
under the treatment of a Doctor at Bahula Colliery Dispensary. No Notice of enquiry was served upon him by the 
Enquiry Officer. He was not even verbally informed about the Charge Sheet and the date of enquiry, as such he was 
unable to attend the enquiry and the Enquiry Officer concluded the enquiry exparte. Eventually, the Enquiry Officer 
submitted his report and the General Manager of the Area approved the Order of dismissal against him bearing No. 
GM:SBA:96/777 dated 8/22.0.996. After receiving the order of dismissal, Sushil Bouri requested the 
management for allowing him to join his duty but the management did not accommodate him. According to the union 
the punishment of dismissal from duty for a period of three months and twenty days is disproportionate to the charge 
levelled against him. Union prayed for setting aside the order of dismissal of the workman and to reinstate him in 
service with full back wages and all other consequential benefits. 


3.Management contested the Industrial Dispute. In their written statement it is admitted that Sushil Bouri was a 
permanent employee of ECL. According to the management Sushil Bouri was absent from duty without any 
authorization. Charge Sheet was issued against him under Clause 26.23 and 26.29 of the Certified Standing Orders of 
the company. The charge employee did not submit any representation or reply against the Charge Sheet. The 
management initiated a Domestic Enquiry and gave him opportunity to defend himself but the workman did not 
participate in the Enquiry Proceeding. The charge levelled against the workman was proved beyond doubt. The 
Enquiry Officer complied the principles of natural justice and a second Show Cause Notice was issued, giving him 
another opportunity to submit his explanation. The workman did not submit any reply to the second Show Cause 
Notice and the Competent Authority by his letter No. GM:SBA:96/777 dated 8/22.0.l996 terminated the 
workman from his service. After lapse of seventeen years from the date of termination, the workman submitted his 
first representation in the year 204 against the order of termination issued by the General Manager. It is contended 
that due to inordinate delay in raising the Industrial Dispute the case is not maintainable and the management is 
totally justified in dismissing the workman from service for his act of misconduct. In support of their contention the 
management referred a decision of the Hon’ble Supreme Court of India in the case of Nedungadi Bank Limited Vs. 
K. P. Madhavankutty and Others [Appeal (Civil) 638 of 2000]. 


4. The point for consideration before this Tribunal is whether the dismissal of Sushil Bouri is justified, if not whether 
the workman is entitled to reinstatement in service and what other relief he is entitled to? 


5. Sushil Bouri examined himself as Workman Witness No. | and filed an affidavit-in-chief reiterating his case that 
due to illness he was under medical treatment at Bahula Colliery Dispensary situated near his residence and was 
unable to attend his duty from 2!.2.!995. Management issued a Charge Sheet against him on |/!3.04.996. He 
replied to the Charge Sheet and requested for allowing him to join duty. There is no evidence of service of Notice of 
enquiry. The Enquiry Officer conducted an ex-parte enquiry and the management dismissed him from service of the 
company without granting him any opportunity to prove his case. After receiving the information of his dismissal, he 
again appealed before the management to allow him to join his duty but themanagement did not consider his appeal. 
The witness further stated that for absence of three months and twenty days the management awarded extreme 
punishment of dismissal against him which is unjustified. The workman stated that he may be join his duty and of 
back wages should be paid. Workman filed the following documents in support of his case : 


(i) Copy of the Medical documents, consisting of four pages for the period from December, 995 to June, 996 is 
produced as Exhibit ४४-।. 


(ii) Copy of Order of dismissal dated 8/22.0.996, as Exhibit W-2. 


6. In cross-examination the witness deposed that he joined his service in August, 984 and he admitted that he 
submitted a reply to the Charge Sheet along with medical documents. Witness denied that Notice of enquiry was 
issued to him asking him to attend the enquiry. He also denied that he was not prevented from joining his duty due to 
illness or he intentionally did not participate in the Enquiry Proceeding. 


7. Mr. Rahul Rao, Assistant Manager (Personnel) was examined as Management Witness No. |. Witness stated in his 
affidavit-in-chief that Sushil Bouri of Sonepur Bazari Project was chargesheeted for his unauthorized absence under 
Clause 26.23 and 26.29 of the Certified Standing Orders of the company. The employee did not submit any reply to 
the Charge Sheet. The 


employee was given opportunity to defend his case but he did not participate in the Enquiry Proceeding. Charge 
levelled against the ex-employee was proved beyond doubt and after following the principles of natural justice a 
second Show Cause Notice was issued but the employee did not turn up. The Competent Authority thereafter 


[भाग ave 3(ii)] भारत का राजपत्र : मई 3, 2025/ज्येष्ठ 0, 947 379 


dismissed the workman by issuing letter dated 8/22.0.996. It is stated that the first representation against dismissal 
was made by the General Secretary of Koyala Mazdoor Congress in the year 204, after lapse of seventeen years from 
the date of termination and due to such inordinate delay in raising the Industrial Dispute the same is liable to be 
dismissed. The management witness examined for the first time on 08.08.2023 but failed to produce any 
authorization. On 20.!.2023 examination-in-chief of Management Witness No. | was resumed and he produced the 
Service Record Excerpt of Sushil Bouri as Exhibit M-! and Order of dismissal, issued by the General Manager, 
Sonepur Bazari Area, ECL is produced as Exhibit M-2. On 30.08.2024 the examination-in-chief of management 
witness was resumed, he stated that he was unable to produce any copy of Charge Sheet, Notice of enquiry, 
Appointment letter of the Enquiry Officer, Enquiry Proceeding, Findings of the Enquiry Officer, and second Show 


Cause Notice. He produced a copy of General Diary bearing No. 369 dated 27.07.2022 lodged before the 
Pandaveswar Police Station as Exhibit M3, wherein it was mentioned that that one file of Disciplinary Proceedings 
related to dismissal of Sushil Bouri, ExEP Fitter, is found to be missing and cannot be traced from Vocational 
Training Centre of the company. 


8. It transpires from his cross-examination that Sushil Bouri was absent from duty for three months and twenty days. 
The witness admitted that punishment of dismissal against Sushil Bouri is disproportionate to the nature of 
misconduct committed by him. 


The stage is set for examining whether the order of dismissal issued against Sushil Bouri is tenable under the facts and 
circumstances of the case and to what relief the workman is entitled to? 


0.Mr. Rakesh Kumar, Union representative argued that the workman was unable to attend his duty from 2!.2.995 
to .04.996 for a period of three months and twenty days due to illness. The management of Sonepur Bazari Project 
without issuing any Notice of enquiry and second Show Cause Notice dismissed the workman, denying him the 
opportunity to defend his case. It is argued that the workman had an unblemished past record but the management 
dismissedhim in illegal manner. The union representative submitted that at present the workman is fifty-nine (59) 
years of age and he may be reinstated in service on payment of his back wages. 


.Mr. P. K. Das, learned advocate for the management submitted that except the order of dismissal the management 
witness failed to produce any document as the file relating to Disciplinary Proceedings of Sushil Bouri wasfound 
missing from the custody of the management and a general diary was lodged before Pandaveswar Police Station 
bearing No. 369 dated 27.07.2022, which has been produced as Exhibit M-3. Learned advocate argued that 
undisputedly the workman was absent from duty for a long time without any information and a Charge Sheet was 
issued against him for his unauthorized absence from 2.2.995 to 3.04.996 and after holding enquiry the 
workman was dismissed. It is further argued that the workman was aware about the letter of dismissal dated 
8/2.0.996 issued against him, which was communicated to him under registered post with A/D at his home 
address at Vill. and PO: Bahula, Dist.: Burdwan, but the workman did not make any representation before the 
management. It is only in the year 2022 a delayed Industrial Dispute was raised by the union without assigning any 
reason for such delay. Learned advocate urged that the dismissed workman is not entitled to any relief in this case and 
that Industrial Dispute is liable to be dismissed. 


2. I have considered the Industrial Dispute referred to this Tribunal in the light of the pleadings of the parties, 
evidence adduced by the workman and management and argument advanced on behalf of their respective parties. It is 
crystal clear that management has not been able to produce any copy of Charge Sheet disclosing the charge levelled 
against the workman. No Charge Sheet, no Notice of enquiry, no order of appointment of the Enquiry Officer, no 
Enquiry Proceeding, no Findings of the Enquiry Officer, and no Second Show Cause Notice could be produced by the 
management. Both parties have produced a copy of order of dismissal dated I8/22.0.996 issued by the General 
Manager, Sonepur Bazari Area, ECL, dismissing the workman from service with immediate effect and the workman 
is directed to collect his legal dues from the Project Officer after submission of necessary document or papers. 
The management of ECL has miserably failed to discharge their burden of proof that a fair Enquiry Proceeding 
was conducted for considering the charge. The order of dismissal cannot be sacrosanct without any tangible evidence 
of holding a fair domestic enquiry. At a later stage management has produced a copy of General Diary (G.D.E. No. 
369 Exhibit M3) entry made before Pandaveswar Police Station dated 27.07.2022, which has been marked as 
Exhibit M3. The content of the General Diary disclose that one file of Disciplinary Proceedings related to dismissal of 
Sushil Bouri, ExEP Fitter, U.M. No. 7064! of Sonepur Bazari Project is found missing and could not be traced at 
Vocational Training Centre, where it had been kept. The missing diary does not exempt the management from their 
discharging burden of proof that the workman was guilty of the charge for unauthorized absence and habitual absence 
from duty. The courts have consistently held that the object of principles of natural justice, which are now understood 
as synonymous with the obligation to provide a fair hearing, is to ensure that justice is done and there is no failure of 
justice. Therefore, without evidence of a proper Enquiry Proceeding held against the workman, it cannot be presumed 
that he was guilty. 


3.In the case of Sajila P.K Vs. Kerala Public Service Commission [2025:KER:5997], the Hon’ble High Court of 


3720 THE GAZETTE OF INDIA : MAY 3], 2025/JY AISTHA 0, 947 [PART II—SEC. 3(ii)] 


Kerala held that : 


“When reviewing disciplinary actions against employees, Courts or Tribunals should consider whether violations of 
rules or regulations are substantive or procedural. Violation of substantive provisions, such as those related to the 
competency of the authority imposing punishment, typically requires strict compliance, and thus, the test of prejudice 
has no role. Procedural violations, on the other hand, should be examined to determine whether they prejudiced the 
employee's ability to defend himself. If prejudice is found, the order has to be set aside. Otherwise, no interference is 
necessary.” In the instant case the dismissed workman in his affidavit-in-chief has stated that he could not attend his 
duty due to illness w.e.f. 2.2.I995 and after recovery he reported for his duty and submitted treatment papers 
from the doctor of Bahula Colliery Dispensary of ECL but the management did not consider his request and issued a 
Charge Sheet dated |/3.04.996 to him. The workman appears to have admitted receipt of the Charge Sheet and he 
also stated that he replied to the Charge Sheet, requested the management to allow him to join his duty. Be that as it 
may, no Notice of enquiry was issued to him. The workman was not informed about the Enquiry Proceeding, which 
was conducted in his absence and without providing him the opportunity to defend himself and without supplying the 
copy of Enquiry Proceeding and Findings of the Enquiry Officer was dismissed from service. It therefore transpires 
that the workman was prejudiced by not being able to submit his medical documents before the Enquiry Officer and 
stand the test of cross-examination by the Management Representative. The order of dismissal issued by the 
Competent Authority against the workman is not tenable in a case when such order is not fortified by the report of 
Enquiry Officer. The workman produced documents relating to his treatment at Bahula Colliery Dispensary from 
22.2.995 till 30.2.995 and from Central Hospital Kalla from 08.0.996 till 26.06.!996. During cross- 
examination of the workman no objection was raised against the medical documents collectively produced as Exhibit 
W-i. Under such facts and circumstances, I hold that the management of Sonepur Bazari Project has committed 
illegality in the matter of dismissal of the workman from service and the order of dismissal bearing No. 
GM:SBA:96/777 dated 8/22.0.996 issued by the General Manager, Sonepur Bazari Area, terminating the 
workman from his service with immediate effect is not sustainable under the law and the same is set aside. 


4. I find from the materials in record that after the order of dismissal was passed, the workman did not file any 
Mercy Petition nor did he submit any representation before the management for reinstatement. It is only on 
5.05.204 that an Industrial Dispute was initiated which resulted in Failure of Conciliation on 6.02.2022. There is 
no evidence on record that the workman made himself available for any duty of the management from 996 to May, 
204. The Industrial Dispute has been raised after an inordinate delay of eighteen years. There is no iota of evidence 
adduced on record that the workman was not gainfully employed during these eighteen years. In such view of the 
matter, I am not inclined to extend any benefit of back wages to the workman till 5.05.204. I find it just and 
appropriate to direct reinstatement of the workman if he has not crossed the age of superannuation. The appropriate 
relief in my considered view is payment of a lumpsum compensation of thirty percent (30%) of back wages to the 
workman from 5.05.204 till the date of his superannuation or the date of his reinstatement, whichever is earlier. The 
management of the company is also directed to pay the workman his legal dues within two (2) months from the date 
of communication of the Award. 


Hence, 
ORDERED 


that the Industrial Dispute is allowed in part on contest against the management of Sonepur Bazari Project under 
Sonepur Bazari Area of Eastern Coalfields Limited. The order of dismissal bearing No. GM:SBA:96/777 dated 
8/22.0.996 issued by the General Manager, Sonepur Bazari Area, is set aside. Sushil Bouri, the workman be 
reinstated in his service under ECL. He is allowed a lumpsum compensation of thirty percent (30%) of his back wages 
from 5.05.20/4 till the date of his superannuation or reinstatement whichever is earlier along with all other legal 
dues. Management of ECL shall pay all dues to the workman within two (2) months from the date of communication 
of the Award. Let an award be drawn up in light of my above findings. Let copies of the Award in duplicate be sent to 
the Ministry of Labour, Government of India, New Delhi for information and Notification. 


ANANDA KUMAR MUKHERJEE, Presiding Officer

(son of Late Bablu Murmu) 

Vs 
Management of Naba Kajora Colliery, ECL

For the Union/Workman: Mr. Rakesh Kumar, President, Koyala Mazdoor Congress
